title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
one_line: Dense but rewarding; it helps to already know what a cognitive bias is and to be comfortable with simple probability.
summary: Kahneman's account of the two systems that drive how we think: the fast, intuitive System 1 and the slow, deliberate System 2.

before.title: Predictably Irrational
before.author: Dan Ariely
before.why: Introduces the same biases through quick, funny experiments, so Kahneman's formal treatment feels familiar.

before.title: The Undoing Project
before.author: Michael Lewis
before.why: Tells the story of Kahneman and Tversky, which gives the ideas in the big book a human thread to hang on.

before.title: Nudge
before.author: Richard H. Thaler
before.why: Applies the biases to everyday choices before you meet the underlying theory.

after.title: Noise
after.author: Daniel Kahneman
after.why: Kahneman's follow-up on the other source of bad judgment: inconsistency.

after.title: Superforecasting
after.author: Philip E. Tetlock
after.why: Puts the ideas to work on prediction and shows how to actually get better at it.

after.title: Judgment under Uncertainty
after.author: Daniel Kahneman
after.why: The original research papers, for readers who want the source.

title: Gödel, Escher, Bach
author: Douglas R. Hofstadter
one_line: The most-abandoned book on many shelves. You want a working idea of formal systems and self-reference before you start.
summary: A Pulitzer-winning exploration of how meaning and self-awareness can arise from formal systems, braided through dialogues, puzzles, Bach and Escher.

before.title: Logicomix
before.author: Apostolos Doxiadis
before.why: A graphic novel about the quest for logical foundations; painless way to meet Russell, Gödel and the questions GEB plays with.

before.title: Gödel's Proof
before.author: Ernest Nagel
before.why: A short, clear walk through the incompleteness theorem that GEB assumes you can follow.

before.title: I Am a Strange Loop
before.author: Douglas R. Hofstadter
before.why: Hofstadter's own clearer restatement of GEB's central message, written because readers missed it.

after.title: The Mind's I
after.author: Douglas R. Hofstadter
after.why: Essays and stories on self and consciousness, curated with Dennett.

after.title: Metamagical Themas
after.author: Douglas R. Hofstadter
after.why: The Scientific American columns, for readers who want more of the same mind.

title: Sapiens
author: Yuval Noah Harari
one_line: Readable, but it moves fast across 70,000 years; a light timeline of human history in your head helps.
summary: A sweeping history of humankind from the cognitive revolution to the present.

before.title: A Short History of Nearly Everything
before.author: Bill Bryson
before.why: Gives you the deep-time scaffolding that Sapiens assumes, told with jokes.

before.title: Origin Story
before.author: David Christian
before.why: Big-history framing of the same arc with clearer signposts.

after.title: Homo Deus
after.author: Yuval Noah Harari
after.why: The sequel, turning the same lens on the future.

after.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
after.author: Jared Diamond
after.why: The deeper argument about why societies diverged.

after.title: The Dawn of Everything
after.author: David Graeber
after.why: A demanding counter-argument to Harari's story of early societies.

title: The Black Swan
author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
one_line: Taleb assumes you can tell a bell curve from a fat tail; the before-line gets you there gently.
summary: On the extreme impact of rare, unpredictable events and our blindness to them.

before.title: The Drunkard's Walk
before.author: Leonard Mlodinow
before.why: A friendly tour of randomness and probability intuition, the ground Taleb stands on.

before.title: Fooled by Randomness
before.author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
before.why: Taleb's earlier, shorter book with the same ideas in simpler clothes.

after.title: Antifragile
after.author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
after.why: What to do about black swans: build things that gain from disorder.

after.title: The Signal and the Noise
after.author: Nate Silver
after.why: Prediction in practice, with the humility Taleb demands.

title: The Selfish Gene
author: Richard Dawkins
one_line: Clear prose, but it assumes natural selection is already comfortable for you.
summary: Evolution seen from the gene's point of view.

before.title: Why Evolution Is True
before.author: Jerry A. Coyne
before.why: The plainest account of natural selection, which Dawkins takes as given.

before.title: The Greatest Show on Earth
before.author: Richard Dawkins
before.why: Dawkins on the evidence for evolution; warms you up to his style before the theory.

after.title: The Blind Watchmaker
after.author: Richard Dawkins
after.why: How complexity arises without a designer; the natural companion.

after.title: The Extended Phenotype
after.author: Richard Dawkins
after.why: Dawkins's own pick as his most important book, and the hardest.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
one_line: Short, but every page assumes a passing acquaintance with relativity and quantum ideas.
summary: Hawking's account of the universe, from the big bang to black holes.

before.title: Astrophysics for People in a Hurry
before.author: Neil deGrasse Tyson
before.why: The vocabulary of the cosmos in an afternoon.

before.title: Seven Brief Lessons on Physics
before.author: Carlo Rovelli
before.why: Relativity and quantum theory as seven short, beautiful essays.

after.title: The Order of Time
after.author: Carlo Rovelli
after.why: Goes deeper on what Hawking means by time.

after.title: The Fabric of the Cosmos
after.author: Brian Greene
after.why: Space, time and the texture of reality, in more detail.

after.title: Black Holes and Time Warps
after.author: Kip S. Thorne
after.why: The full story of black holes from a Nobel laureate.

title: The Intelligent Investor
author: Benjamin Graham
concepts: what a stock and a bond are
one_line: The classic, but 1949 prose and balance sheets; come with the basics of stocks, bonds and fees.
summary: Graham's foundational text on value investing and the margin of safety.

before.title: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing
before.author: John C. Bogle
before.why: The fundamentals of markets, costs and index funds in plain words.

before.title: One Up on Wall Street
before.author: Peter Lynch
before.why: How to think about individual companies before Graham's stricter method.

before.title: A Random Walk Down Wall Street
before.author: Burton G. Malkiel
before.why: The academic case about prices you'll want to weigh against Graham.

after.title: The Most Important Thing
after.author: Howard Marks
after.why: Modern value-investing judgment from a practitioner.

after.title: Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits
after.author: Philip A. Fisher
after.why: The growth-investing counterpart Buffett pairs with Graham.

after.title: Security Analysis
after.author: Benjamin Graham
after.why: Graham's full professional treatment.

title: Capital in the Twenty-First Century
author: Thomas Piketty
one_line: A big economics book with charts on every page; you need the vocabulary of income, capital and growth first.
summary: Piketty's analysis of wealth and income inequality across two centuries.

before.title: Economics: The User's Guide
before.author: Ha-Joon Chang
before.why: A plain-language map of economics that explains the terms Piketty uses without stopping.

before.title: The Undercover Economist
before.author: Tim Harford
before.why: Economic reasoning in everyday situations; builds the intuition.

before.title: Naked Economics
before.author: Charles Wheelan
before.why: Macroeconomics without equations.

after.title: The Price of Inequality
after.author: Joseph E. Stiglitz
after.why: A Nobel laureate's take on the same question from the policy side.

after.title: Capital and Ideology
after.author: Thomas Piketty
after.why: The even larger sequel.

title: Deep Learning
author: Ian Goodfellow
one_line: A graduate textbook. Linear algebra, probability and some calculus are assumed from chapter one.
summary: The standard reference on deep learning, from the mathematical foundations to research topics.

before.title: Make Your Own Neural Network
before.author: Tariq Rashid
before.why: Builds one neural network by hand with school maths; nothing is assumed.

before.title: Grokking Deep Learning
before.author: Andrew W. Trask
before.why: The intuition for gradients and backprop, in code before symbols.

before.title: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow
before.author: Aurélien Géron
before.why: The practical bridge: you'll have trained real models before the theory arrives.

after.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
after.author: Richard S. Sutton
after.why: The next pillar of the field, with the same rigour.

after.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
after.author: Kevin P. Murphy
after.why: The broader probabilistic view of everything Goodfellow covers.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
one_line: The book every backend engineer is told to read; it assumes you've already run a database in anger.
summary: The big ideas behind reliable, scalable and maintainable data systems.

before.title: Learning SQL
before.author: Alan Beaulieu
before.why: You need to be fluent in queries before chapters on storage engines make sense.

before.title: Database Design for Mere Mortals
before.author: Michael J. Hernandez
before.why: Schema thinking without the distributed-systems weight.

before.title: Web Scalability for Startup Engineers
before.author: Artur Ejsmont
before.why: A gentler first pass over caching, replication and queues.

after.title: Fundamentals of Software Architecture
after.author: Mark Richards
after.why: Zooms out from data systems to whole-system trade-offs.

after.title: Database Internals
after.author: Alex Petrov
after.why: Opens up the storage and consensus machinery Kleppmann describes.

title: Clean Architecture
author: Robert C. Martin
concepts: one real project's worth of experience
one_line: Approachable if you've written and tested a few programs; abstract if you haven't.
summary: Martin's principles for structuring software so it stays easy to change.

before.title: Clean Code
before.author: Robert C. Martin
before.why: The function-level habits this book scales up to systems.

before.title: The Pragmatic Programmer
before.author: David Thomas
before.why: The working engineer's mindset the architecture advice assumes.

after.title: Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture
after.author: Martin Fowler
after.why: The catalogue of patterns Martin references.

after.title: Domain-Driven Design
after.author: Eric Evans
after.why: The deep end of modelling a business in code.

title: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions
author: Thomas S. Kuhn
concepts: examples from the history of physics
one_line: Short and famous, but it argues with philosophers you may not have met.
summary: Kuhn's account of paradigms and how science actually changes.

before.title: Philosophy of Science: A Very Short Introduction
before.author: Samir Okasha
before.why: The questions and names Kuhn is responding to, in 140 pages.

before.title: What Is This Thing Called Science?
before.author: A. F. Chalmers
before.why: The standard undergraduate primer that sets Kuhn in context.

after.title: The Logic of Scientific Discovery
after.author: Karl Popper
after.why: The view Kuhn pushed against.

after.title: Against Method
after.author: Paul Feyerabend
after.why: Where the argument goes if you keep pulling the thread.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
one_line: A private notebook, not a treatise; it reads far better once you know what a Stoic was trying to do.
summary: The emperor's private reflections on living well.

before.title: How to Think Like a Roman Emperor
before.author: Donald J. Robertson
before.why: Marcus's life and the Stoic method, so the notes make sense.

before.title: A Guide to the Good Life
before.author: William B. Irvine
before.why: Stoicism as a practice, in modern terms.

after.title: Letters from a Stoic
after.author: Seneca
after.why: The same philosophy in letters, warmer in tone.

after.title: Discourses and Selected Writings
after.author: Epictetus
after.why: The teacher behind Marcus's notes.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
one_line: You can start today. Nothing needs to come first.
summary: A practical system for building good habits and breaking bad ones.

after.title: The Power of Habit
after.author: Charles Duhigg
after.why: The science behind the habit loop Clear builds on.

after.title: Tiny Habits
after.author: BJ Fogg
after.why: The research lab version of the same method.

after.title: Deep Work
after.author: Cal Newport
after.why: What to do with the habits once you have them.

title: Why We Sleep
author: Matthew Walker
one_line: Written for everyone; no preparation needed.
summary: The science of sleep and why it matters.

after.title: The Circadian Code
after.author: Satchin Panda
after.why: Timing of light, food and sleep, applied.

after.title: Breath
after.author: James Nestor
after.why: The other overlooked basic of the body.

title: The Emperor of All Maladies
author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
one_line: A page-turner, but it is long and assumes you can follow talk of cells, genes and trials.
summary: A biography of cancer.

before.title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
before.author: Rebecca Skloot
before.why: Cells, research ethics and medical history through one family's story.

before.title: Being Mortal
before.author: Atul Gawande
before.why: Medicine from the patient's side; shorter and just as humane.

after.title: The Gene
after.author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
after.why: Mukherjee's next history, on heredity.

after.title: The Song of the Cell
after.author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
after.why: The third in the trilogy.

title: The Singapore Story
author: Lee Kuan Yew
concepts: outline of Singapore's path to independence
names of the main political parties and figures
one_line: Long and detailed; a short history of Singapore first will make the names and dates land.
summary: Lee Kuan Yew's memoirs up to 1965.

before.title: Singapore: A Biography
before.author: Mark Ravinder Frost
before.why: A readable, illustrated history that gives you the backdrop for the memoir.

after.title: From Third World to First
after.author: Lee Kuan Yew
after.why: The second volume, 1965 to 2000.

after.title: Hard Truths to Keep Singapore Going
after.author: Lee Kuan Yew
after.why: Interviews late in life; the same mind looking back.

title: Thinking in Systems
author: Donella H. Meadows
one_line: A gentle primer; you can begin here.
summary: How to see stocks, flows and feedback loops everywhere.

after.title: The Fifth Discipline
after.author: Peter M. Senge
after.why: Systems thinking applied to organisations.

after.title: Limits to Growth
after.author: Donella H. Meadows
after.why: The famous model behind the primer.

title: The Code Book
author: Simon Singh
one_line: Written for curious general readers; start here.
summary: The history of secret writing from ancient Egypt to quantum cryptography.

after.title: Serious Cryptography
after.author: Jean-Philippe Aumasson
after.why: The modern mathematics behind the stories.

after.title: Applied Cryptography
after.author: Bruce Schneier
after.why: The professional reference.

title: Introduction to Algorithms
author: Thomas H. Cormen
one_line: The university reference; it is a wall unless you can already read a proof and write a loop.
summary: The comprehensive textbook on algorithms.

before.title: Grokking Algorithms
before.author: Aditya Y. Bhargava
before.why: Illustrated, friendly, and covers the core ideas in a weekend.

before.title: Algorithms
before.author: Robert Sedgewick
before.why: Code-first treatment of the same material; the proofs come later.

before.title: The Algorithm Design Manual
before.author: Steven S. Skiena
before.why: Practical, war-story style; bridges to CLRS's rigour.

after.title: Concrete Mathematics
after.author: Ronald L. Graham
after.why: The mathematics CLRS leans on.

after.title: The Art of Computer Programming, Volume 1
after.author: Donald E. Knuth
after.why: Where the field's rigour comes from.

title: The Phoenix Project
author: Gene Kim
one_line: A novel; anyone who has worked near IT can start it today.
summary: A novel about IT, DevOps and helping your business win.

after.title: The DevOps Handbook
after.author: Gene Kim
after.why: The non-fiction version of what the novel shows.

after.title: Accelerate
after.author: Nicole Forsgren
after.why: The research evidence for the practices.

after.title: Site Reliability Engineering
after.author: Betsy Beyer
after.why: How Google runs it at scale.

title: The Wealth of Nations
author: Adam Smith
one_line: Eighteenth-century prose and a thousand pages; meet Smith through a guide first.
summary: The founding text of modern economics.

before.title: The Worldly Philosophers
before.author: Robert L. Heilbroner
before.why: Smith and the economists after him as people and ideas, in one readable book.

before.title: Adam Smith: What He Thought, and Why It Matters
before.author: Jesse Norman
before.why: A guide to the arguments you are about to read in the original.

after.title: The Theory of Moral Sentiments
after.author: Adam Smith
after.why: Smith's other half; the ethics behind the economics.

after.title: The Great Transformation
after.author: Karl Polanyi
after.why: The most influential reply to the market society Smith described.
